bio: I build machine learning models and the software that puts them to work on noisy, high-dimensional biological data. I hold a B.S. in Computer & Information Science and an M.S. in Biology, and have spent nine years developing methods in research groups at HHMI, Fred Hutch, and the University of Oregon.

I work across the whole modeling lifecycle and the infrastructure around it: encoding data, fitting models in PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow, validating them on simulated and experimental data, and shipping open-source packages and pipelines that run at scale on HPC clusters and AWS. My [skills page](https://jaredgalloway.com/skills/) shows where I've used each tool.

That work has contributed to more than 20 publications with 1,800+ citations, in journals including *Cell*, *eLife*, and *Molecular Biology and Evolution*. My [research page](https://jaredgalloway.com/research/) collects the papers that best represent it, with figures, code, and documentation. Most recently I built transformer models of natural selection in viral proteins; my [experience page](https://jaredgalloway.com/experience/) covers each role in detail.
I left the Matsen Lab in August 2026 and am looking for my next role in applied machine learning. I explain technical results clearly to collaborators of every background.
